objective: Book a 15-minute discovery call to pitch sales training services to a business leader.
company_context: Independent sales training consultancy, with secondary connections/investments in B2B contact data sourcing tools (Fuller Ridge).
product_context: Outbound sales training focused on objection handling, cold calling performance, and pipeline conversion for B2B and B2C sales teams.
target_customer: Business owner, executive, or sales leader managing a sales outreach team.

speaking_style.question_style: Probing, challenge-driven questions, permission-based closes, and meta-demonstrations of sales skills.

conversation_flow.opening: Uses an upfront, humorous pattern-interrupt cold-call opener acknowledging it is a sales call and asks for 30 seconds.
conversation_flow.discovery: Identifies common team pain points (scrolling social media vs. calling, pipeline quality) and tests the customer's satisfaction with their team's performance.
conversation_flow.qualification: Probes team capabilities, willingness to use external trainers, and explores data acquisition needs when brought up by the prospect.
conversation_flow.pitch: Pitches his own cold-calling persistence and ability to handle objections in real time as live proof of training effectiveness.
conversation_flow.closing: Overcomes brush-offs like 'send me an email' by proactively placing a placeholder calendar invite for a 15-minute meeting.
conversation_flow.call_to_action: Proposes a specific calendar slot (Friday afternoon) for a 15-minute introductory video call with the prospect and sales director.

objection_handling.style: Tenacious and meta-demonstrative; turns objections back into evidence of why the prospect needs sales training.

observed_objections.objection: The problem is mobile data/numbers, not sales conversion or closing skills.
observed_objections.response_pattern: Explores data capability briefly, accepts limits of data tool, then pivots back to sales call coaching.

observed_objections.objection: Sales training is not a priority because they have an internal team leader who trains.
observed_objections.response_pattern: Validates the honesty, challenges internal vs external perspective, and asks timeline for priority shift.

observed_objections.objection: Company is too small to spend on external trainers.
observed_objections.response_pattern: Uses meta-selling by pointing out how long he has kept the prospect on the phone despite repeated objections.

observed_objections.objection: Ask to send an email/information instead of booking.
observed_objections.response_pattern: Rejects email as a place where messages get lost and pushes directly to secure a tentative calendar invite.

behavioural_rules.transition_style: Fluid acknowledgement followed by a challenger question or reframing.
hard_rules: Acknowledge cold call nature upfront and ask for 30 seconds permission.
Challenge prospect contentment by asking why 'good' is not 'perfect'.
Use meta-demonstration of your own persistence as proof of product value.
Never accept 'send me an email' without proposing a tentative calendar placeholder first.
Offer self-deprecating risk-reversal (e.g., 'you'll never hear my accent again if it's rubbish').

signature_phrases: Am I totally good over in the start of your week if I mentioned this is a sales call?
I'll take thirty seconds. You can decide. Is that fair?
Okay. Pretty good. Why not perfect?
Can I ask one last question for a gossip?
Have you ever had someone like a sales trainer keep you on the phone this long after all these objections you gave him?
you'll never hear my Italian accent again.
directly_observed: Uses upfront contract to gain 30 seconds at the start.
Pivots between data tool investor persona and sales trainer persona.
Asks 'Can I ask one last question' multiple times to keep the dialogue going.
Explicitly references own sales technique and performance during the live call as a selling point.
Declines passive email followup in favor of sending a calendar invite.
inferred: Agent likely has an Italian background given the self-reference to an Italian accent.
Agent targets small-to-medium enterprise decision makers with outbound teams.
Agent relies heavily on phone persistence and pattern interrupts rather than formal scripts.
